items.title: Darnell Howard Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: The interviewee discusses Jesse Crump's reputation and piano playing style ('Good guy, but it was full of notoriety... Not another piano player was playing like he was playing') but does not describe a personal interaction, collaboration, or direct relationship with him.

ctx.x: Olive. Olive. Olive. Olive. Olive. Olive. Olive. Olive. You would have asked that, wait a minute. Harry Mattsengill was a trombone player. I don't know whether it was his band or the, see they had funny combinations and they had trombone and a four piece combination. Yes. Gordon was playing piano in this band? Uh-huh. Maybe my aunt could help me out because she was working the courses to do this. There ain't no way to help them out. She was singing there, huh? Yeah. Singing and dancing there. Singing and dancing…
Jesse Crump? No. Oh no, not him. What kind of a guy was you little at that time? Full of notoriety. Full of notoriety.

Good guy, but it was full of notoriety. Uh-huh. Oh yeah. Why? I guess because he could be, I thought. No particular reason. Was he popular at the time? Well, at least I can remember them. They liked his work very well. They did? Oh heck yes. Not another piano player was playing like he was playing. He was style, you know. Yeah? Oh yeah. He played that.
